rmt-2005-calc-01.title: Maximize the profit
rmt-2005-calc-01.body:
Profit $=nD-\text{cost}=n(110-2n)-(600+10n+n^2)=-3n^2+100n-600$. The real maximum is at $n=\frac{100}{6}=16\frac23$, so check the nearest integers: $n=16$ gives $232$ and $n=17$ gives $233$. The best is $n=17$.

**Answer: 17 statues**

rmt-2005-calc-02.title: Iterate the relation
rmt-2005-calc-02.body:
The relation gives $f(2x+1)=2f(x)$. Take $x=-1+\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon$ small. Then $2x+1=-1+2\varepsilon$, and after $k$ steps we are at $-1+2^k\varepsilon$ with $f(-1+2^k\varepsilon)=2^kf(-1+\varepsilon)$. Choose $\varepsilon=2^{1-k}$, so that $-1+2^k\varepsilon=1$: then $f(1)=2005=2^kf(-1+2^{1-k})$, so $f(-1+2^{1-k})=2005\cdot2^{-k}\to0$. If the limit exists it must be $0$.

**Answer: 0**

rmt-2005-calc-03.title: Optimize the area
rmt-2005-calc-03.body:
Let $x$ be the radius and $y$ the height of the rectangle (width $2x$). Perimeter: $\pi x+2x+2y=24$, so $y=12-\frac{(\pi+2)x}{2}$. Area: $A=\frac\pi2x^2+2xy=24x-\left(2+\frac\pi2\right)x^2$. Setting $A'=24-(4+\pi)x=0$ gives $x=\frac{24}{4+\pi}$, a maximum since $A''<0$. Then $y=12-\frac{(\pi+2)}{2}\cdot\frac{24}{4+\pi}=\frac{12(4+\pi)-12(\pi+2)}{4+\pi}=\frac{24}{4+\pi}$.

**Answer: radius $=$ height $=\frac{24}{4+\pi}$ ft**

rmt-2005-calc-06.title: Maximize the angle
rmt-2005-calc-06.body:
Let $x$ be the distance from the screen. The top is 36 ft above eye level and the bottom 6 ft, so the angle is $\theta=\arctan\frac{36}{x}-\arctan\frac6x$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{36/x-6/x}{1+216/x^2}=\frac{30x}{x^2+216}$. (The official solution writes $\frac{42x}{\dots}$; the correct numerator is $30x$.) The angle is largest where $\frac{30x}{x^2+216}$ is largest: its derivative is zero when $x^2=216$, so $x=6\sqrt6\approx14.7$ ft.

**Answer: $6\sqrt6$ feet**

rmt-2005-calc-06.title: Circle theorem
rmt-2005-calc-06.body:
The angle subtended by the screen is largest at the point of the horizontal line through the eye where a circle through the top and bottom edges of the screen is tangent to the line. By the tangent-secant theorem, $x^2=6\cdot36=216$, so $x=6\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt6$ feet**

rmt-2005-calc-07.title: Logarithmic differentiation
rmt-2005-calc-07.body:
$\ln f=x\ln x$, so $\frac{f'}f=\ln x+1$ and $f'(x)=x^x(1+\ln x)$. This is negative for $x<\frac1e$ and positive for $x>\frac1e$, so the minimum is at $x=\frac1e$.

**Answer: $\frac1e$**

rmt-2005-calc-09.title: Integration by parts
rmt-2005-calc-09.body:
$\int\delta'(x)\sin x\,dx=\big[\delta(x)\sin x\big]_{-\infty}^{\infty}-\int\delta(x)\cos x\,dx=0-\cos0=-1$, since $\delta$ vanishes away from $0$.

**Answer: $-1$**

rmt-2005-calc-10.title: Differentiate geometric series
rmt-2005-calc-10.body:
Split $i(i+1)=i(i-1)+2i$. Then $\sum i(i-1)p^{i-2}=\frac{d^2}{dp^2}\frac1{1-p}=\frac2{(1-p)^3}$ and $\sum ip^{i-2}=\frac1p\cdot\frac{d}{dp}\frac1{1-p}=\frac1{p(1-p)^2}$. The sum is $\frac2{(1-p)^3}+\frac2{p(1-p)^2}=\frac{2p+2(1-p)}{p(1-p)^3}=\frac2{p(1-p)^3}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2}{p(1-p)^3}$**
